anomalies.observed: On both servo headers, pin 1 is wired to the servo power rail (D2 cathode, feeding C1/C4/C6/C6) and pin 2 is wired to GND. Pin 3 carries the signal path (through R230/R160 and the 0 Ω serial jumpers R13/R14), which matches the spec.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that D2 feeds 'J3/J8 pin 2' (the servo power rail) and that pin 3 is the signal pin, implying pin 1 = GND, pin 2 = V+, pin 3 = signal — the standard hobby-servo connector convention. The schematic has pins 1 and 2 swapped: V+ on pin 1, GND on pin 2.

evidence.quote: D2 | PMEG3030EP Schottky | Diode from +5V into the servo power rail (feeding J3/J8 pin 2 and the C1–C4 bank)
J3, J8 | Conn_01x03 | Servo header, channel 1 (J3) and channel 2 (J8). Pin 3 is the signal pin
Sheet m5-pantilt, page 1: D2 (PMEG3030EP) cathode connects to the servo power rail; the rail wire enters J8 at pin 1 (top) and J2 at pin 1 (top), while GND connects to J8 pin 2 and J2 pin 2.

anomalies.impact: A standard 3-pin servo cable (SG90-class: brown=GND on pin 1, red=V+ on pin 2, orange=signal on pin 3) plugged into either header would receive reversed power polarity, likely damaging the servo immediately. In serial mode the same reversed-polarity issue applies to RS304MD/RS30X servos on the shared bus.

parsed.summary: The servo headers J8 and J2 show the power and ground pins swapped relative to the specification: the schematic routes D2's servo power rail to pin 1 and GND to pin 2, whereas the spec states D2 feeds pin 2 (with pin 1 as GND). This would reverse supply polarity on any standard servo cable plugged into either header.
